A1.pain: Every click costs money and the phone stays silent — he pays for visitors, not jobs.
A1.noa_pick: 0 — the taxi price question is instant Israeli recognition and 'the only driver who pays the passengers' is the best punchline in A; concept 2 (the employee) is the safe runner-up.

concepts.logline_en: Dash explains that his campaign is a taxi where every passenger asks the price to the airport and leaves — and the driver pays for the question.
concepts.story_he: דשוני מסתכל על בעל הבית שסופר קליקים כמו מונה מונית, ומסביר לו שכל קליק הוא נוסע שנכנס, שואל ״כמה עד נתב״ג?״, שומע מחיר ויוצא — והוא משלם על השאלה. הנהג היחיד בארץ שמשלם לנוסעים. ואז דשוני מראה לו את בוט המודעות של WAO, שלומד רק מהעבודות שהוא סימן כסגורות, לא מכל מי שנכנס לשאול.
concepts.joke_en: The laugh is the inversion — 'the only driver in the country who pays the passengers' — landing right after the perfectly ordinary taxi question 'how much to Ben Gurion?', so the ear recognises the scene before the absurd verdict hits.
concepts.callback_en: The airport question from the first beat returns as the filter at the end: the bot counts only rides that reached a closed job, not every head in the door.
concepts.why_this_lands_en: Every tradesman has paid for 'interest' that never became work, and every Israeli knows the taxi price question by heart.
concepts.noa: Connected: one analogy carried through, though it explains more than it escalates. 'The only driver in the country who pays the passengers' is a native, ear-proof punchline. No rule breach. Fixed: the product line now uses a relative clause instead of a dash fragment, and the calque 'כל ראש בדלת' became the callback 'כל מי שנכנס לשאול'.

concepts.logline_en: The owner installs a dealership-style sales bell and rings it for every click, until the bell is hoarse and the phone is still silent.
concepts.story_he: בעל הבית תולה פעמון מכירות ליד הדשבורד ומצלצל על כל קליק, כמו בסוכנות רכב, ועד הצהריים הפעמון צרוד והטלפון שלו — דממה. דשוני, יבש — הפעמון התאמן, הטלפון לא. ואז הוא מראה לו את בוט המודעות של WAO, שלומד מהעבודות שהוא מסמן כסגורות, לא מהקליקים.
concepts.joke_en: The escalation is audible — ding, ding, ding all morning — and the punchline personifies the bell as the only thing that got a workout, a dry two-part contrast that needs no screen.
concepts.callback_en: The bell from the opening returns in the verdict 'the bell trained, the phone didn't', and the end replaces it with the only count that matters: jobs he marks closed.
concepts.why_this_lands_en: He knows the dealership bell ritual, and he knows the feeling of a busy day that produced nothing.
concepts.noa: Escalation works by ear (ding all morning), but the premise is imported: Israeli dealerships don't ring a sales bell, so he won't recognise the ritual. 'הפעמון התאמן, הטלפון לא' is weak in Hebrew; a 'hoarse bell' doesn't land. For Tamar: needs a local ritual and a sharper verdict. No rule breach.

concepts.logline_en: Dash asks whether he'd keep an employee who charges for every passer-by that looks at the van — then reveals the campaign is that employee.
concepts.story_he: דשוני שואל את בעל הבית שאלה אחת: עובד שמביא אנשים שמסתכלים על הרכב והולכים, ולוקח כסף על כל מבט — היית מפטר אותו? ״תוך דקה״, הוא עונה. אז דשוני מסביר שהקמפיין הוא בדיוק העובד הזה, ומציג את בוט המודעות של WAO, שלומד מהעבודות שסגרת בפועל, לא ממבטים.
concepts.joke_en: The laugh is the trap — he answers 'fired in a minute' like any boss, then the reveal makes him the boss of that idiot employee; the question-and-answer rhythm works purely by ear.
concepts.callback_en: 'Would you fire him?' opens the story and closes it: the bot is the worker you keep, because it learns only from jobs you actually closed.
concepts.why_this_lands_en: He judges workers by results all day; turning that exact standard on his own ads is the recognition and the joke at once.
concepts.noa: Connected: question, his answer, then the trap, all of it dialogue and fully eyes-closed. Comparing the campaign to an employee who charges for lookers is within the rules. Funny as a trap, though it gets a nod more than a laugh. Fixed 'התשובה ברורה, תוך דקה' (unnatural) to his own spoken answer. Keep the callback 'the worker you keep' clear of any implied guaranteed calls when it's scripted.

A2.pain: The budget burns out again on clicks that land, look around and leave — traffic, never customers.
A2.noa_pick: 0 — the shuk tasting crowd is the exact pain (lookers who never buy), fully by ear, and the tasters-vs-buyers callback maps straight onto marked closed jobs; concept 2 is funnier but its product doesn't fix its pain.

concepts.logline_en: Dash compares the campaign to a shuk stall handing out free tastings: the tasters keep coming back with friends, and nobody ever buys.
concepts.story_he: דשוני מסביר לבעל הבית שהקמפיין שלו הוא דוכן טעימות בשוק: כולם טועמים, חוזרים, מביאים חברים — והקופה ריקה. הקהל השמין, הקופה לא. ואז הוא מראה לו את בוט המודעות של WAO, שלומד מהעבודות שהוא סימן כסגורות, לא ממי שרק טעם.
concepts.joke_en: The laugh is the punchline contrast 'the crowd got fat, the till didn't', built on the universally heard shuk call 'come, taste' — the ear fills in the crowd noise without any screen.
concepts.callback_en: The free tasting from the opening returns as the distinction the bot makes: it learns from buyers (closed jobs), not tasters (clicks).
concepts.why_this_lands_en: Every Israeli has watched the shuk tasting crowd eat a stall's profit, and every advertiser has fed that same crowd.
concepts.noa: Connected, very Israeli, eyes-closed safe; 'הקהל השמין, הקופה לא' is a real laugh. Product truth was drifting: 'ממי שבאמת סגר עבודה' made the customer the one who closes the job and dropped the marking. Now 'מהעבודות שהוא סימן כסגורות'. No other breach.

concepts.logline_en: The owner feeds the campaign like a vending machine that eats coins — more coins, bigger bills, a shake — and the display just says thanks.
concepts.story_he: בעל הבית מכניס עוד תקציב לקמפיין כמו למכונה אוטומטית שבולעת מטבעות — עוד מטבע, עוד שטר, ניעור קטן — והמסך מציג ״תודה״. דשוני, בלי למצמץ — המכונה מלאה, הטלפון ריק. ואז הוא מראה לו את בוט המודעות של WAO, שמנהל את הקמפיין בגוגל ולומד רק מעבודות שסגרת וסימנת, לא מהמטבעות שנבלעו.
concepts.joke_en: The escalation is physical and audible — coin, bill, shake, a polite 'thank you' on the display — and the deadpan verdict 'the machine is full, the phone is empty' flips the whole scene in one breath.
concepts.callback_en: The machine's 'thank you' from the opening pays off at the end: the only thank-you that counts is a job he marks closed, and that's what the bot learns from.
concepts.why_this_lands_en: Everyone has shaken a vending machine that ate their coin; every burned advertiser has shaken his budget the same way.
concepts.noa: Connected, with physical escalation. The 'thank you' on the display is a visual beat, so the narration has to say it aloud or the callback dies with the screen off. Same 'X full, Y empty' punchline shape as A1-2, A2-1 and A3-2. No rule breach.

concepts.logline_en: The owner clicks his own ad to check it works, pays for the visit, and Dash congratulates him on being his own best customer.
concepts.story_he: בעל הבית מחפש את עצמו בגוגל ולוחץ על המודעה שלו, רק כדי לבדוק שהיא עובדת — ומשלם על הביקור. דשוני, יבש — מזל טוב, אתה הלקוח הכי טוב של עצמך. ואז הוא מראה לו את בוט המודעות של WAO, שלומד מעבודות אמיתיות שסגרת וסימנת, לא מלחיצות של סקרנים.
concepts.joke_en: The laugh is the mirror — 'congratulations, you're your own best customer' — because every owner has clicked his own ad 'just to check', so the recognition lands before the punchline does.
concepts.callback_en: 'Just checking it works' opens the story; at the end the bot is the thing that actually checks what works — the closed jobs he marks — instead of his own curiosity clicks.
concepts.why_this_lands_en: It's the secret habit every advertiser has and never admits, said out loud in one dry line.
concepts.noa: Best recognition laugh in A2, and it works by ear. But the pain is off-brief (his own click, not strangers who leave), and the product doesn't solve it: learning from closed jobs doesn't stop self-clicks, so the way out doesn't follow from the setup. No rule breach, but a logic gap Eitan will feel.

A3.pain: The agency's glossy reports throw confetti for clicks and impressions while the phone stays silent.
A3.noa_pick: 0 — one question against a wall of proud numbers, then page-flipping and 'הרבה עמודים בשביל ׳אין׳': the most eyes-closed and least forced of the three.

concepts.logline_en: The owner proudly reads the monthly report aloud to Dash — record clicks, green graphs — until one question, 'and customers?', turns it into a lot of pages for 'no'.
concepts.story_he: בעל הבית מקריא לדשוני את הדוח החודשי בהתלהבות — שיא בקליקים, שיא בחשיפות, גרפים ירוקים — ודשוני שואל שאלה אחת: ולקוחות? הוא מדפדף, מדפדף, עוד גרף, ודשוני מסכם — הרבה עמודים בשביל ׳אין׳. ואז הוא מראה לו את בוט המודעות של WAO, שלומד בלי חגיגות מהעבודות שהוא מסמן כסגורות.
concepts.joke_en: The laugh is the deflation — one small question against a wall of proud numbers, answered by the sound of page-flipping and the dry verdict 'a lot of pages for no', all audible.
concepts.callback_en: 'And customers?' is the question the report never answers; the end is the product that starts from exactly that answer — the jobs he marks closed.
concepts.why_this_lands_en: He has sat through that exact presentation, nodded at the graphs, and gone home to a silent phone.
concepts.noa: Connected and fully audible: proud reading, one question, page-flipping, verdict. 'הרבה עמודים בשביל ׳אין׳' is native and dry. No rule breach. The only fix was the dash fragment in the product line.

concepts.logline_en: Every month the agency sends a bigger cake celebrating record clicks, and the owner eats it alone in the van — gaining weight, not customers.
concepts.story_he: כל חודש הסוכנות שולחת לבעל הבית עוגה עם ״מזל טוב על שיא הקליקים״, והוא אוכל אותה לבד ברכב — העוגות גדלות, והטלפון עדיין שותק. דשוני, מסתכל על הפירורים — עלית במשקל, לא בלקוחות. ואז הוא מראה לו את בוט המודעות של WAO, שלומד מהעבודות שסגרת בפועל, בלי עוגות.
concepts.joke_en: The laugh is the absurd escalation made personal — cakes growing while the phone stays silent — and the punchline 'you gained weight, not customers' is a two-part seesaw that needs no picture.
concepts.callback_en: The celebration cake from the opening returns as crumbs in the verdict, and the end swaps the cake for the only celebration that counts: closed jobs he marks.
concepts.why_this_lands_en: He knows agencies that celebrate their own metrics, and he knows the lonely van lunch — the cake just makes it literal.
concepts.noa: Connected absurd escalation; 'עלית במשקל, לא בלקוחות' works by ear. 'Crumbs' and 'growing cakes' are visual, so the voice must name them. Product line says 'שסגרת' with no marking, which is acceptable but weaker than 'סימנת'. No rule breach.

concepts.logline_en: Dash hands the owner a glowing report about his driving — record honking, zero arrivals — and the owner's own outrage becomes the argument against his ads report.
concepts.story_he: דשוני מגיש לבעל הבית דוח על הנהיגה שלו — החלפות נתיב מצוינות, שיא בצפירות, אפס הגעות — ובעל הבית מתעצבן: העיקר להגיע! דשוני, רגוע — זה מה שאני אומר לך על הקמפיין. ואז הוא מראה לו את בוט המודעות של WAO, שלומד מהעבודות שסגרת, לא מהצפירות.
concepts.joke_en: The laugh is the role reversal — he rejects the absurd report with the exact sentence that condemns his real one, 'what matters is arriving', and Dash just hands it back to him.
concepts.callback_en: 'What matters is arriving' is his own line from the middle, and it becomes the product's logic at the end: the bot counts arrivals — closed jobs — not honks.
concepts.why_this_lands_en: Every Israeli driver has an opinion about honkers who go nowhere, and every advertiser has been handed that report in a nicer font.
concepts.noa: Clever role reversal and it works by ear, but the premise is forced (why would Dash grade his driving?), so it takes a beat to land in 30s. Fixed 'הגעות אין' → 'אפס הגעות' and the calque 'מה שמעניין זה להגיע' → the native 'העיקר להגיע!'. Note for scripting: the callback is now 'העיקר להגיע'. No rule breach.

S1.pain: Customers search for his trade right next to his van and can't find him — the job goes to someone two streets away.
S1.noa_pick: 1 — the only S1 concept with true escalation (sign, flag, roof) and a one-line turn ('she's searching Google, not the street') that sets up the product; concept 2 is the pure-audio alternative.

concepts.logline_en: The van is parked exactly under the building with the leak, yet the woman upstairs searching for a plumber finds someone two streets away — the closest man is invisible.
concepts.story_he: הרכב חונה בדיוק מתחת לבניין עם הנזילה, ודשוני מסביר לבעל הבית שאישה למעלה מחפשת עכשיו אינסטלטור — ומוצאת מישהו שני רחובות מכאן. הוא הכי קרוב, והיא בכלל לא רואה אותו. ואז דשוני מראה לו את סייט בוט של WAO — אתר שמכסה את כל השירותים, ופרופיל בגוגל שמספר אותו סיפור.
concepts.joke_en: The laugh is the irony stated flat — physically closest, digitally invisible — and the image of a leak dripping on the van of the man who could fix it works entirely through narration.
concepts.callback_en: 'He's the closest and she can't see him' opens the story; the end is the fix for exactly that — one full story on the site and the profile, where she actually looks.
concepts.why_this_lands_en: Every tradesman has parked under a job he never got, and every one of them knows the neighbour who got it instead.
concepts.noa: A situation more than a story: there is irony but no escalation and no twist, so it's closer to v1 'chunks'. Ambiguity: 'בעל הבית' next to 'הבניין' reads as the building's landlord; for scripting use 'אתה' or another term. Fixed Dash 'looking at the van' (he's inside it) and 'משני רחובות ליד'. No rule breach.

concepts.logline_en: The owner escalates from a bigger magnetic sign to a flag to standing on the roof waving a wrench — while the searcher downstairs keeps finding the competitor on her phone.
concepts.story_he: בעל הבית מגדיל את השלט המגנטי על הרכב, מוסיף דגל, ובסוף עומד על הגג עם מפתח שוודי ומנופף — ואישה שעומדת למטה מוצאת בטלפון את המתחרה. דשוני, מהדשבורד — היא לא מחפשת ברחוב, היא מחפשת בגוגל. ואז הוא מראה לו את סייט בוט של WAO — אתר על כל השירותים ופרופיל שאומר אותו דבר, איפה שהיא באמת מחפשת.
concepts.joke_en: The escalation is pure physical comedy you can hear — sign, flag, wrench on the roof — deflated by one dry sentence, 'she's not searching the street, she's searching Google', the whole lesson in a breath.
concepts.callback_en: The waving wrench on the roof returns as the contrast at the end: stop shouting in the street, say one clear story where the search happens.
concepts.why_this_lands_en: He has invested in signs, magnets and stickers while his Google presence stayed empty — the roof is just the honest ending of that road.
concepts.noa: Connected, with real escalation (sign, flag, roof). 'היא לא מחפשת ברחוב, היא מחפשת בגוגל' is the clearest lesson in the set. The roof and wrench are visual, so narration must describe them, which it does. Fixed 'האישה' (never introduced) and 'במקום שבו' (formal). No rule breach. In the script, don't let 'where she searches' become 'you'll show up first'.

concepts.logline_en: Dash plays today's customer, searches 'plumber nearby', reads out three competitors and says 'calling him' — while the owner shouts 'I'm right here!'
concepts.story_he: דשוני מחליט לשחק היום לקוח: מקליד ״אינסטלטור באזור״, מקריא את התוצאות — המתחרה, עוד מתחרה, ועוד אחד — ואומר ״יאללה, מתקשר אליו״. בעל הבית צועק ״אני פה!״, ודשוני עונה — אז תופיע איפה שהוא מחפש. ואז הוא מראה לו את סייט בוט של WAO — סיפור אחד על כל השירותים, גם באתר וגם בפרופיל בגוגל.
concepts.joke_en: The laugh is the role reversal played straight — the phone becomes the customer and walks away, and 'I'm right here!' is the shout of every invisible business, answered by the one sentence that explains why.
concepts.callback_en: 'I'm right here!' is the opening shout; the end answers it — the site and the profile tell the same full story where the search happens, so 'here' finally means something.
concepts.why_this_lands_en: He has watched someone choose a competitor while standing next to his own van; hearing his phone do it to him is the recognition and the joke.
concepts.noa: Connected and the most eyes-closed concept in S1, because it's pure dialogue. 'אני פה!' is a great shout. Hebrew clean, no fixes. Watch out: 'אז תופיע איפה שהוא מחפש' must not turn into a ranking promise in the script. No rule breach.

S2.pain: Every customer thanks him at the door, but none of it reaches Google — his profile has no reviews.
S2.noa_pick: 2 — the role reversal makes him hear himself say 'later', which is the insight and the laugh at once; concept 0 (door to elevator) is the tighter fallback if 30s gets crowded.

concepts.logline_en: The customer promises a review at the door — 'sure!' — and by the elevator it has evaporated; Dash names the exact distance where thank-yous die.
concepts.story_he: הלקוח בדלת אומר ״הצלת אותי, תודה!״, ובעל הבית מבקש יפה שישאיר לו ביקורת בגוגל. הלקוח מבטיח ״בטח!״, ועד שבעל הבית מגיע למעלית, זה כבר נשכח. דשוני, יבש — בין הדלת למעלית, התודה מתאדה. ואז הוא מראה לו את סייט בוט של WAO, שעוזר ללקוחות שלך להשאיר ביקורת בגוגל, בקלות, לפני שה׳בטח׳ מתאדה.
concepts.joke_en: The laugh is the precise, universally known distance — 'between the door and the elevator, the thank-you evaporates' — a deadpan measurement of something every tradesman has lost exactly there.
concepts.callback_en: The customer's 'sure!' at the door returns at the end: the product catches that 'sure' before the elevator eats it, by making the review easy to leave.
concepts.why_this_lands_en: Every tradesman has heard 'sure, I'll write' and watched it die in the stairwell — naming the elevator makes it his story.
concepts.noa: Connected, tight, eyes-closed; 'בין הדלת למעלית, התודה מתאדה' is a precise, native laugh. Near-breach fixed: 'שיכתוב את זה בגוגל' had him asking the customer to post his exact thank-you (steering content). Now he only asks for a review. Also fixed the logic: the customer is at his own door, so it's the tradesman who walks to the elevator.

concepts.logline_en: To make customers 'tell Google' how good he is, the owner names his dog Google — and now every happy customer pets the dog and says 'good boy, Google', while the profile stays empty.
concepts.story_he: בעל הבית מחליט שכל לקוח יספר לגוגל כמה הוא מקצועי, וכדי שזה יקרה הוא קורא לכלב שלו ״גוגל״ — ועכשיו כל לקוח מרוצה מלטף את הכלב ואומר ״כל הכבוד, גוגל״, והפרופיל בגוגל עדיין ריק. דשוני, בקול שטוח — הכלב אוסף ביקורות, הפרופיל לא. ואז הוא מראה לו את סייט בוט של WAO, שעוזר ללקוחות שלך להשאיר ביקורת בגוגל עצמו, בפשטות.
concepts.joke_en: The laugh is the absurd literalism — 'tell Google' becomes a dog named Google — and the punchline 'the dog collects reviews, the profile doesn't' lands as a clean two-part contrast with a bark built in.
concepts.callback_en: 'Tell Google' from the opening is the wish; the dog is its wrong address, and the end is the right one — a simple way for his customers to leave the review on Google itself.
concepts.why_this_lands_en: He has literally said 'tell Google about me' and watched the thanks go everywhere except Google — the dog is that moment with a tail.
concepts.noa: Funniest image in S2, but the premise is unmotivated (why would anyone name the dog to get reviews?), so by ear it's a gag, not a story. The dog also isn't in the van world. Opening line 'יספר לגוגל כמה הוא מקצועי' is his wish, not our method, so it stays within the review rule, but don't carry 'how professional' into the product line. No rule breach.

concepts.logline_en: His own AC breaks, the tech does great work, and the owner says 'thanks, you saved me!' and walks away — until Dash asks 'and the review?' and he hears himself say 'I'll get to it later'.
concepts.story_he: המזגן של בעל הבית מתקלקל, הטכנאי עושה עבודה מעולה, ובעל הבית אומר לו בדלת ״תודה, הצלת אותי!״ וסוגר את הדלת. דשוני שואל: וביקורת? הוא עונה ״אחר כך אני אכתוב״, ודשוני אומר — עכשיו אתה מבין את הלקוחות שלך. ואז הוא מראה לו את סייט בוט של WAO, שעוזר ללקוחות שלך להשאיר ביקורת, לפני ש׳אחר כך׳ הופך ל׳אף פעם׳.
concepts.joke_en: The laugh is the mirror — he becomes his own forgetful customer, and 'now you understand your customers' lands because the ear just heard him say the exact line he's been hearing for years.
concepts.callback_en: 'I'll get to it later' is his line from the middle; the end is the product that makes sure 'later' doesn't become never, by making the review easy right after the job.
concepts.why_this_lands_en: Every tradesman has also been the customer who meant to write and didn't — hearing himself do it is the smile.
concepts.noa: Connected role reversal with the strongest insight in S2: he hears himself say the line he hates. Works by ear. Fixes: 'והולך' (he's at his own home, so he closes the door), the stiff 'אחזור לזה אחר כך' → 'אחר כך אני אכתוב', and the calque 'ש׳אחר כך׳ נהיה אף פעם' → 'הופך ל׳אף פעם׳'. No rule breach.

S3.pain: His site says electrician, his profile says plumber, the customer wants AC — three stories, so Google and customers can't tell what he does.
S3.noa_pick: 1 — answering 'כן' to an either/or question is a joke every Israeli already owns, it's pure dialogue, and 'כן זה לא מקצוע' leads straight into one story across site and profile.

concepts.logline_en: The man who re-levels a shelf three times until the bubble sits dead centre lives with a business that's three different professions online — and Dash won't let him keep both standards.
concepts.story_he: בעל הבית מיישר מדף שלוש פעמים עד שהבועה בפלס יושבת באמצע, אבל ברשת העסק שלו הוא שלושה מקצועות שונים — באתר חשמלאי, בפרופיל אינסטלטור, והלקוחה בכלל חיפשה מיזוג. דשוני, יבש — מדף עקום אתה לא מוכן לקבל, אבל את זה כן. ואז הוא מראה לו את סייט בוט של WAO — אתר ופרופיל בגוגל שמספרים אותו סיפור על כל השירותים, והבועה חוזרת לאמצע.
concepts.joke_en: The laugh is the craftsman's own standard turned on him — 'a crooked tile you won't accept, but this you do' — and the level bubble is described, not shown, so the ear sees it.
concepts.callback_en: The bubble jammed to one side opens the story and centres at the end, when the site and the profile finally tell one story about all his services.
concepts.why_this_lands_en: Precision is his pride; showing him the one place he tolerates a crooked line is the recognition and the joke together.
concepts.noa: Connected and sharp on his pride, but it lands as a smile, not a laugh, and the bubble returning to centre is visual. Fixed the broken list ('a customer looking for AC' isn't a profession) and 'אריח' → 'מדף' so the punchline pays off the shelf he just levelled. No rule breach.

concepts.logline_en: A confused customer calls — the site says electrician, the profile says plumber, so what are you? — and the owner gives the most correct and worst answer: 'yes'.
concepts.story_he: לקוחה מתקשרת מבולבלת: באתר כתוב חשמלאי, בפרופיל אינסטלטור — אז אתה חשמלאי או אינסטלטור? בעל הבית נותן את התשובה הכי נכונה והכי גרועה — ״כן״. היא מנתקת, ודשוני מסביר ש׳כן׳ זה לא מקצוע — ואז מראה לו את סייט בוט של WAO: אתר ופרופיל שאומרים אותו דבר על כל שירות ושירות.
concepts.joke_en: The laugh is the classic 'yes' to an or-question — the most honest answer that explains nothing — and 'yes is not a profession' is a dry verdict that needs only the dialogue, no screen.
concepts.callback_en: 'Yes' opens as the wrong answer and closes as the right one: one story on the site and the profile that says yes to every service he actually offers, in one voice.
concepts.why_this_lands_en: Every multi-service tradesman has been asked 'so what do you actually do?' — and every Israeli has answered 'yes' to a question with 'or' in it.
concepts.noa: Connected, pure dialogue, the most Israeli joke in the set. Meaning fix: the original 'אז מה אתה?' isn't an either/or question, so 'כן' made no sense and the joke died. Now 'אז אתה חשמלאי או אינסטלטור?'. No rule breach (she calls and hangs up, which is the pain, not a call promise).

concepts.logline_en: The owner walks into a clinic where the door says dentist, the diploma says vet, and the doctor says 'open wide' — he flees, and Dash asks how it felt, because that's his customers' experience online.
concepts.story_he: בעל הבית נכנס למרפאה: על הדלת כתוב רופא שיניים, על התעודה וטרינר, והרופא אומר ״תגיד אהה״ — והוא בורח. דשוני שואל אותו איך זה הרגיש, כי ככה מרגישים הלקוחות שלו כשהאתר והפרופיל לא מספרים אותו סיפור. ואז הוא מראה לו את סייט בוט של WAO — אתר ופרופיל בגוגל עם סיפור אחד על כל השירותים.
concepts.joke_en: The laugh is the absurd clinic built from three mismatched signs, capped by 'open wide' from a vet — and the role reversal lands when Dash asks 'how did that feel?', making the owner the confused customer.
concepts.callback_en: The fleeing patient from the opening returns as the question 'how did that feel?' — and the end is the cure: one story on the site and the profile, so nobody has to flee.
concepts.why_this_lands_en: He would never trust a clinic with three identities, and he instantly gets that his customers feel the same about his three online professions.
concepts.noa: Absurd and funny, but it leaves the van world for a clinic and needs three signs listed before the joke, which is heavy for 30s by ear. The explanation line ('because that's how customers feel…') spells out the joke. Fixed 'השירותים' (services don't tell a story) and 'לקוחות' → 'הלקוחות שלו'. No rule breach.
